- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (high sentiment values correlate with forecast overshoots).  
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative or shows strong bearish signals (e.g., sentiment < -0.5, especially after recent highs).  
- Forecast tends to lag mean reversion — prices often correct downward after forecast peaks, especially if sentiment has recently turned negative.  
- When sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days, model overreacts to short-term volatility and overestimates future prices.  
- If sentiment is negative and prices are trending downward, model often fails to fully adjust downward, underestimating the drop.  
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to overconfidence in upward momentum — especially when sentiment is positive and recent prices are rising.  
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, model tends to average out extremes, leading to underestimation of sharp reversals.  
- Correct for “sentiment-driven momentum” — if sentiment is high, reduce forecast by 5–10% for the next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative and prices are falling, model often undercorrects — increase forecast downward by 5–10% to reflect sentiment-driven decline.
